note: Hand-written per-matchup write-ups for the Scores tab, keyed "week|matchup_id", rendered in the click-to-open strip at the foot of each match card. 2026 is written LIVE, week by week -- see Phase 8. Facts sourced from scripts/build_matchup_facts.py; check every number before it goes in. Consolation games with nothing at stake deliberately get no entry.

shape.headline: one line, the game in a sentence
shape.body: 3-4 sentences, Hall of Fame & Shame roast level. Real point figures stay in the prose -- points are a scale everyone reads natively.
shape.tags: optional array of short uppercase labels, e.g. UPSET / BLOWOUT / UNLUCKY LOSS

1|1.headline: SirWinsAlot starts two duds and still posts the best Week 1 score in league history
1|1.body: Jared Hayes scored 214.46 with Colston Loveland at 0.00 and Jaylen Waddle at 0.70 in the lineup and Tyler Shough's 25.20 watching from the bench. Caleb Williams went for 37.26, Ashton Jeanty added 31.20, and a manager who was 0-4 against Jake Blackwell before Sunday won by 68.56. The defending champion got 12.15 from Puka Nacua and 4.10 from Chig Okonkwo, with Pat Freiermuth's 17.10 sitting on the bench.

1|2.headline: Same opponent, same Week 1, nearly the same score, opposite result
1|2.body: A year ago Erin Jacobs opened the season by beating Chris Merkel with 157.29. This year Erin scored 158.23 in the rematch, within a point of it, and lost by 17.86, because Chris started Isaiah Likely at the second tight end spot and got 30.55 back. Derrick Henry went for 35.30 in Erin's opener for the second straight year, and Omarion Hampton answered with 8.30. Mark Andrews managed 10.65, six times last September's output, and nobody is calling it a comeback.

1|3.headline: Matt Bova gets 0.52 from the quarterback spot and a zero from Romeo Doubs
1|3.body: Matt Bova started Sam Darnold, who returned 0.52, and Romeo Doubs, who returned nothing at all, and finished on 85.77, the lowest score of the week. Mike Gesicki's 20.80 sat on the bench, but even the best possible lineup would have come up 33 short. Chris Bova was under projection too, with Bo Nix posting 5.44 and Chuba Hubbard's 22.95 benched, and won by 71.48 anyway behind Jahmyr Gibbs (32.10) and Trey McBride (27.50).

1|4.headline: Nabers in Paris ends an 0-5 run against Duane with a below-median 131.79
1|4.body: Duane Gillenwater had won all five regular-season meetings before Sunday. Nick Bova broke the streak with Christian McCaffrey at 11.55, James Cook — fresh off 8.20 in last year's final — at 8.65, and Dallas Goedert's 26.45 benched behind AJ Barner's 3.55; Jalen Coker's 33.80 covered for all of it. Enter the Maye-Trix got 9.82 from Drake Maye, a rough day for the namesake, and started Jake Ferguson (2.85) over T.J. Hockenson (14.85) in a game lost by 13.44.

1|5.headline: BoKnows723 wins by 108.46, the second-biggest beating in league history
1|5.body: Jake Bogardus got 32.40 from D'Andre Swift in a flex spot, 29.20 from Justin Jefferson, 27.90 from David Montgomery, and 48.62 from Lamar Jackson and Patrick Mahomes at quarterback. Starting Terry McLaurin (2.90) over Kyle Monangai (21.15) was the only blemish. Mitch Blackwell scored 86.06 on Jordan Addison 0.00, Quentin Johnston 3.20, and Jayden Reed 4.25, and the whole bench combined for 33.52, so the answer was not sitting there either.

1|6.headline: Josh Allen scores 37.66 and gets no help whatsoever
1|6.body: Andrew Bova came in as the league's all-time head-to-head leader and got 37.66 from Josh Allen and 16.85 from the entire running back room, with Tony Pollard at 3.40 and George Kittle at 3.70. Nick Merkel got 7.30 combined from Ja'Marr Chase and A.J. Brown and it did not matter: Bryce Young scored 33.44 out of the superflex, more than double the projection, and Bijan Robinson added 29.80. Final: 163.99 to 126.61.

2|1.headline: SirWinsAlot benches the right quarterback again and wins on the wrong ones
2|1.body: Jared Hayes got 7.72 from Caleb Williams and 6.16 from Trevor Lawrence, left Tyler Shough's 22.38 on the bench for the second week in a row, and watched Colston Loveland follow last week's 0.00 with 1.30. It still won by 27.24, because Jonathan Taylor went for 28.45 and three receivers cleared 20. Erin Jacobs got 28.35 from Travis Kelce and 1.10 from Jonathon Brooks in a flex spot, with Tre Tucker's 24.65 sitting on the bench, and 114.49 was never going to cover that.

2|2.headline: Josh Allen finally gets help, and it comes from the tight end room
2|2.body: Andrew Bova started the week 0-2 and scored 174.43, 65.85 above an honest projection: Josh Allen went for 42.82, Dak Prescott added 29.76, and Dalton Schultz (29.75) and George Kittle (20.50) combined for 50.25 at tight end. Nico Collins still sat in the lineup for 0.00. Jake Bogardus scored 134.53, above the median, but David Montgomery managed 3.90 and Justin Jefferson 8.25, and the first loss of BoKnows723's season arrived by 39.90.

2|3.headline: Chris Merkel starts Jaxson Dart for 0.80 and Davante Adams makes it not matter
2|3.body: Chris Merkel had Matthew Stafford's 26.98 on the bench and Jaxson Dart's 0.80 in the lineup, and 128.02 was below the median. Davante Adams saved the day with 40.00. Matt Bova's bench combined for 17.69, so there was no rescue there either, and Devin Singletary (0.90), J.K. Dobbins (3.60) and Tucker Kraft (4.25) left Drew Lock's 23.40 as the best thing in the lineup. At 95.87, Show Me Your Penix posted the week's lowest score for the second straight week.

2|4.headline: Nick Merkel wins with 111.01, a negative from DJ Moore, and 3.00 from Saquon
2|4.body: Breeces Peanut ButterCups scored 20.55 below an honest projection and stayed perfect in head-to-head anyway. Saquon Barkley made 3.00, Bijan Robinson 9.60, DJ Moore finished at -0.10, and Denzel Boston's 20.75 watched from the bench. Duane Gillenwater could not take advantage: Drake Maye (8.02) and Carson Wentz (6.32) combined for 14.34 at quarterback, and Enter the Maye-Trix is 0-4.

2|5.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba scores 42.00 and Mitch Blackwell still loses by 80
2|5.body: Mitch Blackwell got 42.00 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and 20.02 from Cam Ward, and 3.85 from the whole running back room, with Mike Washington at 0.70. Jayden Reed (0.90), Alec Pierce (2.10) and Quentin Johnston (2.15) rounded out a 99.73. Chris Bova scored 180.11 on CeeDee Lamb's 34.55 and 51.40 from his backs, left just 11.75 on the table, and is 4-0.

2|6.headline: The defending champion beats Nick Bova for the first time in five tries
2|6.body: Jake Blackwell was 0-4 against Nabers in Paris before Sunday and scored the week's best 181.29 to end it: Jared Goff (29.78) and Brock Purdy (28.48) at quarterback, 34.20 from Amon-Ra St. Brown, 26.20 from DeVonta Smith. Nick Bova benched Dallas Goedert for 26.45 last week, started him this week for 1.40, and left Darren Waller's 19.55 on the bench. Malik Nabers, the team's namesake, scored 0.60, and 138.43 lost by 42.86.

3|1.headline: Matt Bova wins one, and it takes two quarterbacks and a Mitch Blackwell to do it
3|1.body: Show Me Your Penix got 45.14 from Sam Darnold (26.66) and Jordan Love (18.48) plus 20.75 from Tee Higgins, and the first win of the season arrived at 130.94, still below the median. Hunter Henry scored 1.75 in the flex with Mike Gesicki's 13.70 on the bench. Mitch Blackwell beat an honest projection by 37.69 and got 34.36 from Jaxon Smith-Njigba, then lost by 12.46 with one quarterback in the lineup, Cam Ward at 9.44, and Emari Demercado starting for 0.00. Mitch is 0-6, and Matt now leads the all-time series 3-1.

3|2.headline: Jake Blackwell's two Brocks score 64.63, and Duane Gillenwater's quarterbacks score 9.88
3|2.body: Nacua Matata scored 182.44, a second straight week over 180, with Brock Purdy at 33.28, Brock Bowers at 31.35 and Michael Wilson at 23.65, and Jacoby Brissett's 25.60 still sat on the bench. Duane Gillenwater got 3.76 from Drake Maye and 6.12 from Jameis Winston, started T.J. Hockenson for 3.60 with Kenyon Sadiq's 26.75 on the bench, and left 51.28 on the table, the most of the week. Enter the Maye-Trix is 0-6, and the all-time series is level at 2-2.

3|3.headline: Nick Merkel benches Geno Smith's 26.04 and loses by 1.74
3|3.body: Breeces Peanut ButterCups started Malik Willis for 10.00 with Geno Smith's 26.04 on the bench, a 16.04-point swap that would have covered a 1.74-point loss nine times over. Bijan Robinson went for 35.80 and Ja'Marr Chase 23.30, while Brian Thomas made 1.55 and Terrance Ferguson 2.15. Jake Bogardus scored 133.78, 0.10 below the median, on 29.40 from Drake London and 5.20 from Justin Jefferson, and took the head-to-head win anyway to go 3-2 all-time against Nick.

3|4.headline: SirWinsAlot finally starts Tyler Shough, and nobody can catch it
3|4.body: After two weeks of benching him, Jared Hayes started Tyler Shough and got 23.80, plus 19.78 from Trevor Lawrence and 24.55 from Juwan Johnson, for 157.53. Jonathan Taylor followed last week's 28.45 with 8.20 and it did not matter. Chris Merkel scored 133.99, 0.11 above the median, and lost by 23.54 with Marcus Mariota's 20.42 on the bench behind Baker Mayfield's 13.28 and 13.55 from his two running backs combined. Hayes is 6-0; Chris Merkel still leads the all-time series 3-2.

3|5.headline: Nick Bova posts the week's low and hands the family series to Andrew
3|5.body: Nabers in Paris scored 103.41, 40.31 below an honest projection: De'Von Achane made 1.70, Adonai Mitchell 0.00, Daniel Jones 7.90, and Malik Nabers, the namesake, 5.85 after last week's 0.60. Kirk Cousins (22.22) and Christian McCaffrey (21.35) were the only reasons it cleared 100. Andrew Bova won by 40.64 on George Kittle's 29.20 and Jaylen Warren's 20.35, despite starting Blake Corum for 2.00 with Konata Mumpfield's 20.05 and Aaron Rodgers' 22.68 on the bench, and now leads the all-time series 3-2.

3|6.headline: Chris Bova scores 235.30, and Erin Jacobs' fourth-best score of the week loses by 91
3|6.body: Titsburg Feelers posted the second-highest regular-season total in league history, behind a 246.52 from 2023: Jahmyr Gibbs went for 40.40, Kyren Williams, Bhayshul Tuten and Chuba Hubbard added 50.05 more, and Harold Fannin (25.85) and Trey McBride (18.75) made 44.60 at tight end. That was 73.87 above an honest projection. Erin Jacobs beat the median with 144.26, got 21.75 from Matthew Golden and 21.40 from Derrick Henry, and lost by 91.04. Chris Bova is 6-0 and 3-1 all-time against her.
